summary: David Drewes is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Lawrence University, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and the University of Virginia, he later taught at Virginia, Indiana University (attested 2006), and the University of Manitoba (attested 2008–2010).

David E. Cooper is a philosopher who studied at Highgate School and St Edmund Hall. He was a lecturer at Oxford (1967), Professor of Philosophy at Durham University (1986–2008), and Distinguished International Visiting Professor at Peking University (2022).

David E. Riggs works in Japanology and Buddhist studies. After earning his Ph.D. at UCLA, he taught at UC Santa Barbara, UIUC, and the University of Hawaiʻi, and held research posts at Nichibunken (attested 2006) and Oberlin College (attested 2010).

David F. Germano is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992 and served as Associate Professor of Tibetan and Buddhist Studies at the University of Virginia (attested 2000–2008).

David Faure is a historian and sinologist. He studied at the University of Hong Kong and Princeton University, taught at Indiana University, lectured at St Antony's College (1990–2006), and served as a director at the Chinese University of Hong Kong (~2006).

David Fiordalis specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. Educated at Carleton College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Michigan (PhD attested 2008), he became associate professor and chair of religious studies at Linfield University (attested 2017).
David Friedman was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He served as Reader in Indian Philosophy at SOAS (~1950–1970) and as Professor at the University of London (~1965–1970).
David Gonsalez is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Lobsang Choephel, Lati Rinpoche, Kirti Tsenshab Rinpoche, and Denma Lochö Rinpoche.

David Gordon White is an Indologist and historian of religion. He studied at Wisconsin, Banaras Hindu University, the Sorbonne, and the University of Chicago (PhD ~1988), later holding professorships at the University of Virginia and UC Santa Barbara.

David J. Kalupahana was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at the University of Ceylon and SOAS (PhD ~1966), he lectured at the University of Ceylon (~1962–1971) and chaired the philosophy department at the University of Hawaiʻi (1972).

David Jones is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Hawaiʻi. Attested in 2007, he served as professor of philosophy in the University System of Georgia and directed the Center for the Development of Asian Studies.

David K. Wyatt was a historian educated at Harvard, Boston University, and Cornell (PhD ~1966). He taught at SOAS (~1962–1968) and the University of Michigan (~1968–1969) before serving as chair of history at Cornell University (1969–2002).
David Kerman Tomlinson is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. Supervised by Dan Arnold, he earned his PhD from the University of Chicago (attested 2019) and held a post at Smith College.
David Kopf was a scholar of history and Indology who studied at the University of Chicago (~1960–1964) and held a faculty post at the University of Minnesota (~1967–1997).
David L. Gosling is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held a Spalding Fellowship at Clare Hall, Cambridge in 1992 and held a post at the University of Cambridge (attested 2001).

David L. Haberman is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Colorado (~1971–1976) and held academic posts at the University of Arizona (~1989–1993) and Indiana University (~1993).

David L. McMahan works in Buddhist and religious studies. After teaching at UC Santa Barbara and the University of Vermont, he served as an assistant professor (attested 2002) and later Professor of Religious Studies (attested 2013) at Franklin & Marshall College.

David Llewellyn Snellgrove was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Southampton and Cambridge, he was a Professor at SOAS and the University of London (1950–1982) and founded the Institute of Tibetan Studies, Tring.

David Ludden is a historian and Indologist educated at Yale and the University of Pennsylvania. He taught at Virginia (1979–1980), the University of Pennsylvania (1981–2008), and became Professor of Political Economy and Globalization at NYU in 2007.

David M. DiValerio is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the School for International Training and the University of Virginia (PhD attested 2011), later holding a post at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee (attested 2015).
